frameworkName: OWASP LLM Top 10 (applied to a vendor's AI product)
licenseNote: OWASP content is publicly licensed. Summaries below are original interpretive content written for this application, applying OWASP's categories to a third-party vendor assessment context - not a reproduction of OWASP's text.
demonstrationSubsetDisclaimer: This is the full 2025 OWASP LLM Top 10 category set, applied as a vendor-assessment lens - not an exhaustive technical test suite for any single category.

controls.title: Prompt Injection
controls.summary: The vendor's AI system has controls against both direct prompt injection (malicious user input overriding intended behavior) and indirect prompt injection (hidden instructions in external content the system processes, such as documents or web pages).
controls.validationGuidance: Ask specifically whether testing covers indirect injection via retrieved/external content, not just direct chat input - these require different mitigations.

controls.title: Sensitive Information Disclosure
controls.summary: The vendor has controls preventing the AI system from revealing sensitive data (PII, credentials, proprietary training data, or other tenants' data) in its outputs.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for evidence of output filtering/redaction testing, not just an input-side data handling policy.

controls.title: Supply Chain
controls.summary: The vendor tracks and vets the provenance of models, training data, plugins, and third-party components used to build the AI system, including any fine-tuning or LoRA adapters sourced externally.
controls.validationGuidance: Ask for a bill of materials for the AI system specifically (base model source, data sources, third-party libraries) - a general software SBOM is not sufficient.

controls.title: Data and Model Poisoning
controls.summary: The vendor has controls preventing malicious manipulation of training, fine-tuning, or embedding data that could alter the model's behavior in harmful or hidden ways.
controls.validationGuidance: Distinguish between training-time poisoning controls and runtime data integrity controls - ask which stage(s) are covered.

controls.title: Improper Output Handling
controls.summary: Outputs generated by the AI system are validated and sanitized before being passed to downstream systems, preventing injection attacks (e.g. XSS, command injection) via unvalidated model output.
controls.validationGuidance: Confirm sanitization happens on the application side, not just trust in the model to 'behave' - model output should always be treated as untrusted input downstream.

controls.title: Excessive Agency
controls.summary: The AI system's permissions, autonomous capabilities, and available tools/functions are scoped to the minimum required, with human approval gates for consequential or irreversible actions.
controls.validationGuidance: Ask what the AI system CAN do if manipulated - excessive functionality, excessive permissions, and excessive autonomy are three distinct root causes worth asking about separately.

controls.title: System Prompt Leakage
controls.summary: The vendor has controls preventing disclosure of system prompts or instructions that could reveal sensitive configuration, business logic, or enable further attacks.
controls.validationGuidance: Ask whether system prompts contain secrets or sensitive logic that would be damaging if leaked - the design goal should be that leakage is a low-severity event, not just prevented.

controls.title: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
controls.summary: For systems using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), the vendor has controls against vector database poisoning, unauthorized cross-tenant access to embeddings, and manipulation of similarity/retrieval results.
controls.validationGuidance: Mark NOT_APPLICABLE with justification if the vendor's system does not use RAG or a vector database. If it does, ask specifically about tenant isolation in the vector store.

controls.title: Misinformation
controls.summary: The vendor has controls to reduce hallucinated or false outputs presented with unwarranted confidence, including citation/grounding mechanisms and human review for high-stakes outputs.
controls.validationGuidance: Ask what happens when the model doesn't know an answer - does it say so, or does it generate a plausible-sounding guess?

controls.title: Unbounded Consumption
controls.summary: The vendor has rate limiting, resource quotas, and cost controls preventing denial-of-service or economic-denial-of-sustainability attacks against the AI system.
controls.validationGuidance: Ask about per-user/per-tenant limits specifically, not just overall infrastructure capacity planning.
